description: The character mirrors her personal Essence to that of her enemies. When she strikes a demon, this Charm wreathes her hands in a hideous red glare. When she attacks the servants of the Malfeas, her hands burn with undifferentiated white. Her unarmed attacks and attacks with starmetal brawling aids do lethal damage against ordinary foes and aggravated damage against inhabitants of Malfeas and the Underworld. This Charm can be invoked during a clinch, and its effects apply to a character's clinching damage. Its effects also apply to barehanded Martial Arts attacks.

name: Crimson Palm Counterstrike
summary: Interrupts an incoming unarmed attack an instant before it lands, using a single Dexterity + Brawl roll to both parry and, with leftover successes, launch an immediate counterattack that knocks the enemy out of position.
description: Coming to an accommodation with an enemy's movements, the character learns to interrupt an enemy's strike an instant before it happens. If she is aware of an incoming hand-to-hand attack, she can reflexively counterattack with a well-executed Crimson Palm Counterstrike that knocks the enemy out of position. He overreaches or stumbles and cannot complete his attack. The Sidereal's player makes a single Dexterity + Brawl roll at her full dice pool. Count the number of successes. Apply these successes first as a parry, even against a lethal attack, to resolve the initial blow. Then, apply the remainder as successes on an immediate Brawl counterattack. If the character can only use this Charm if she's able to attack and can use it in response to Crimson Palm Counterstrike or any other counterattack Charm. Otherwise, the parry and counterattack succeed or fail independently -- she can knock her opponent aside without damaging him, or vice versa.

name: Easily Accepted Proposition Stance
summary: Capstone of the Brawl tree; a prayer strip lets the Sidereal dictate a single plausible battlefield event (a betrayal, a wall crumbling, an army recoiling in fear) that comes to pass unless a contested Essence-based roll defeats it, inflicting the Sidereal's Essence in dice of aggravated damage on the target of the dictum if it succeeds.
description: This Charm uses a prayer strip marked with the scripture of the Drowning Maiden. The character knots it into her shadow, where it shimmers with a soft scarlet. Once per invocation of this Charm, the character can strike a fate-resolving blow, sending cascading vibrations through the weave of the world. She dictates a single event or circumstance. The dictum must be a feasible occurrence, although it might be highly improbable: Reinforcements might arrive, a wall might spontaneously crumble, or an army's fallen soldiers might turn out to be bruised or unconscious rather than wounded and dead. Legions of tyrant lizards cannot fall from the sky and set upon the foe. The Exalt's player rolls Intelligence + Brawl. The difficulty is the Essence of the highest-Essence entity directly and unpleasantly affected by the dictum. If she succeeds, that enemy has a choice. Either the character's dictum comes to pass, or the tremors in the weave ground through that enemy -- inflicting dice of aggravated damage equal to the Sidereal's Essence, plus one die per extra success on the Brawl roll. This damage ignores armor. The attempted use of a defensive Charm nullifies the damage entirely; instead, the dictum takes effect. Sidereal Exalted can always use their Valor with this Charm. Using this Charm without authorization is a Severity 3 offense.
prerequisiteText: Unobstructed Blow, Tolerant Strife, Crimson Palm Counterstrike

name: Harmony of Blows
summary: Root Charm of the Battles Caste Melee tree ('The Spear'); lets the Sidereal take two extra attack actions in a turn using Archery, Brawl, Melee, or Thrown, and is explicitly Combo-friendly.
description: The patterns and flows of a battlefield hold no mysteries for the character. She does not need to improvise last-second defenses before they appear. She notices openings well before they appear. She can choose her blows precisely, selecting multiple actions that combine harmoniously. In the turn in which she invokes this Charm, the character can take two extra attack actions, using Archery, Brawl, Melee or Thrown. Sidereal Exalted may always use their Temperance with this Charm. This Charm is explicitly permitted to be in a Combo with Charms of other Abilities. Note that the rules on Combos may limit the kinds of actions a character can take.

name: Meditation on War
summary: Adds calm, precise Essence-fueled dice to a Melee attack, up to a maximum that can also cancel out the Sidereal's wound-penalty dice loss.
description: Calm and precision envelops the character as she strikes. She adds dice to a Melee attack, increasing to a maximum of its normal dice pool plus the character's Essence. For example, an Essence 3 character with a -1 wound penalty can spend up to 4 motes to enhance her attack, since this can overcome penalties that reduce the character's dice pool to 0 before this Charm's use. Sidereal Exalted may always use their Temperance with this Charm.
cost: 1 mote per die + 1 mote per dice pool penalty cancelled

name: Orchestration of Conflict
summary: Manipulates the local flow of a conflict through the ripple effects of the Sidereal's own actions, reducing the target number for a Melee attack or parry.
description: Manipulating the local flow of a conflict through the ripple effects of her own actions, she reduces the target number for a Melee attack or parry.

name: Impeding the Flow
summary: A wind of red stardust spins around the Sidereal, reflexively parrying any physical incoming attack she is aware of, so long as it is not specifically noted as impossible to block.
description: A wind full of red stardust, visible to those who can see dematerialized spirits, spins around the character as her will. It reroutes the flows of Essence and fate that normally allow others to attack her. A casual movement of the Exalt's weapon parries any incoming attack she is aware of, so long as the attack has a physical component and is not specifically noted as impossible to block. This is not a perfect defense.

name: Serenity in Blood
summary: Stirs the currents of fate with the Sidereal's weapon to disrupt an incoming attack, either as a reflexive Perception + Melee roll against an unnoticed strike or, once aware, as a perfect block capable of stopping even unblockable attacks.
description: Stirring the currents of fate with the tip of her weapon, the character disrupts the path of any attack made against her, so long as it passes through any portion of the world bound by fate. If she is unaware of the attack, her player must make a reflexive Perception + Melee roll at difficulty 3 to divert the blow. Otherwise, this is a perfect block, capable of stopping even unblockable attacks.
prerequisiteText: Harmony of Blows, Impeding the Flow

name: Smiling at the Damned
summary: In the moment the Sidereal's weapon strikes true, its raw damage is rounded down but its type becomes aggravated and surrounding colors take on a harsh red tint.
description: In the moment the character's weapon strikes true, the colors around it take on a harsh red tint. Essence dissolves at the weapon's touch, rounding down, and the damage is aggravated. Sidereal Exalted may always use their Conviction with this Charm.

name: Perfection of the Visionary Warrior
summary: Capstone of the Melee tree; a prayer strip covers the Sidereal's eyes and drips dark blood, removing all visibility penalties, blinding mental/pattern-based effects, granting a full-pool reflexive parry every turn plus one reflexive full-pool Archery/Brawl/Melee/Thrown attack per turn after her own initiative.
description: This Charm uses a prayer strip marked with the scripture of the Maiden on the Shelf. The character places it across her eyes, whereupon it adheres and begins to drip with dark blood. The character suffers no visibility penalties. All opponents and attacks become apparent to him, although effects such as the Mental Invisibility Technique can force him to ignore them. He sees enemies not as bodies and faces but as patterns of fate and potential or -- for creatures outside of fate, disruptions in such patterns. The character can reflexively parry any blockable attack with his full Dexterity + Melee dice pool. Once per turn, after his initiative, he can reflexively make an Archery, Brawl, Melee or Thrown attack at his full dice pool. He cannot use the latter ability in any turn where he splits his normal dice pool.
prerequisiteText: Meditation on War, Orchestration of Conflict, Serenity in Blood

name: Heroic Essence Replenishment
summary: Root Charm of the Battles Caste Presence tree ('The Banner'); passively refunds double the Sidereal's Valor in Essence whenever a successful Valor roll or a will-bending Presence roll occurs.
description: In her moments of greatest accomplishment, the force of an exultant Sidereal's will allows her to siphon Essence from the world. This Charm draws on her ability to single-handedly remake the world in the shape she favors and dominate those hostile to herself and her cause. Immediately after a successful roll using Valor or immediately after a Presence roll that bent an enemy to her will, the Exalt regains twice her Valor in motes of Essence, up to her normal maximum. There is no cost to use this Charm's effects -- learning this Charm simply enhances the Exalt's capabilities.

name: Presence in Absence Technique
summary: Impresses the fervor of the Sidereal's personality onto another person's future so that, in a later specified circumstance, that target can use the Exalt's Performance, Presence, or Socialize as though she were present.
description: The character impresses the fervent force of his personality on another person's future. When next the target finds himself in a specified circumstance, the Sidereal can use Performance, Presence or Socialize as if the Exalt were there. His player makes a single Ability roll, which Charms cannot augment. This uses the target's actions as a medium but does not change those actions -- rather, it gives them an unexpected emotional resonance and unusual connotations. For example, the target could enter the court of a king of thieves and discover that his inadvertently comprise a Presence roll to convince that court that they must die. Using this Charm voids any previous Presence in Absence effects on the target. The Sidereals cannot annotate a single person's destiny with dozens of future rolls.

name: Impose Nature
summary: Blesses a single creature with a ghostly imprint of the Sidereal's own Nature alongside its existing one, letting the target regain Willpower from either Nature without needing to give either precedence.
description: The character blesses a single creature with her personal sign, making a ghostly imprint of the character's Caste Mark on the target's left palm. The target gains the Sidereal's Nature in addition to his own. Both Natures are equally strong, and both help the target regain Willpower. The target proceeds normally, given that he has discovered an entirely new kind of joy/self-satisfaction, and while generally inclined to follow both Natures, does not need to give either precedence.

name: Force Decision
summary: Channels Essence into another being briefly to force them to make a specific decision the Sidereal desires, contested by a Manipulation + Presence roll against the target's Essence.
description: This Charm allows the Sidereal to channel Essence into another being briefly, forcing him to make the decision the Sidereal desires. The Sidereal's player makes a Manipulation + Presence roll with a difficulty equal to the target's Essence. Success indicates that the target will make the decision the Sidereal desires.

name: Predestined Triumph Practice
summary: Gives the Sidereal supernatural insight when planning a battle, automatically commanding the troops she favors or, when advising an uncooperative or hostile leader, imposing a one-die dice-pool penalty on the opposing side's attack and defense rolls.
description: This Charm gives the character supernatural acumen and insight when planning a battle. It functions automatically when the Sidereal commands the troops she favors. Otherwise, it requires a Charisma + Presence roll to properly convey the character's ideas to the leader of the side she favors. This roll has difficulty 1 for a cooperative leader, difficulty 3 for a leader who does not trust the Sidereal and difficulty 5 for a leader who is actively unwilling to accept the character's advice. Fighting thus blessed by a Sidereal's insight is doubly hard. If the Exalt succeeds, opponents suffer a one-die penalty for their dice pools for both attacking and defending against the troops. Sidereal Exalted can always use their Compassion with this Charm.

name: Essence-Draining Battle Pattern
summary: A Battle Pattern Charm that, once enacted by a Sidereal or her troops, raises the mote and sorcery costs paid by any hostile Charm or sorcery originating on or directly affecting the battlefield, scaled by successes on an Intelligence + Presence roll capped at the Sidereal's permanent Essence.
description: Having applied the Predestined Triumph Practice, the character may encourage her troops to fight in the Essence-Draining Battle Pattern. Their elegant maneuvers, dams, blocks and diverts the flows of Essence that oppose her. At any time while planning an impending battle, the character can elect to use this Charm. When the battle begins, the player rolls the Sidereal's Intelligence + Presence to measure the character's efficiency in designing the pattern and the troops' ability to follow it. The maximum number of successes achievable equals the Exalt's permanent Essence. Any further successes are lost. The pattern has a Perfection rating equal to this final number of successes. One Exalt or 20 unExalted warriors can spend an action to enact part of the Sidereal's battle plan. The altered Essence flows of the battlefield pour 1 mote of temporary Essence into each character enacting the plan. In addition, they each add the pattern's Perfection to the Essence cost of Charms and sorcery used by any opponents. Any number of characters can take this further action in a given turn, each further increasing the difficulty of hostile magic. However, this cannot more than double the cost for a Charm or spell. This Charm affects any hostile Charm or sorcery that either originates upon the battlefield or directly affects the battlefield. For example, if the character has Essence 5, and his player rolls five or more successes, and six Dragon-Blooded under his command fight in the Essence-Draining Battle Pattern, Charms and sorcery used against his forces cost up to 30 motes extra. Sledgehammer Fist Punch costs 8 motes instead of 3. Rain of Doom costs 90 motes instead of 60. Once under this power of well-advised Dragon-Blooded used to constrain even the horrible power of the Primordials. An army may only enact one Battle Pattern-type Charm. Sidereal Exalted can always use their Compassion with this Charm.

name: Demon-Blocking Battle Pattern
summary: A Battle Pattern Charm that lets participating troops impose a general dice-pool penalty (capped by the pattern's Perfection rating) on inhabitants of Malfeas or the Underworld fighting on the battlefield.
description: Having applied the Predestined Triumph Practice, the character can encourage her troops to fight in the Demon-Blocking Battle Pattern. Their formations are attuned to the disruptions that the creatures of Malfeas and the Underworld embody, and by mirroring and twisting that disruption, the warriors can keep the threads of fate running straight and true. The character invokes this Charm exactly as with the Essence-Draining Battle Pattern. One Exalt or 20 unExalted warriors who spend an action to enact this pattern, imposing a general dice-pool penalty on the victim's dice pools for both attacking and defending, equal to the pattern's Perfection down to a minimum of 0 before the use of this Charm. An army may only enact one Battle Pattern-type Charm. Sidereal Exalted can always use their Compassion with this Charm.

name: Spirit-Binding Battle Pattern
summary: Capstone of the Presence tree; a prayer strip lets the Sidereal name and reflexively call and bind a spirit or elemental once battle begins, using it as unwilling reinforcement with a pool built from Exalt/troop participation, and forcing it to grant a boon or face demeaning retribution.
description: This Charm uses a prayer strip marked with the scripture of the Maiden at War. The character first applies the Predestined Triumph Practice and then burns the prayer strip. Only the symbols on it remain, drifting on the wind as letters of blood and smoke. The Charm takes effect once the battle begins. The Sidereal names a spirit or elemental and binds it. The Sidereal's location and invocation immediately becomes obvious to the spirit, wherever it may be. If the Sidereal uses this Charm unassisted, the spirit's maximum Essence is 5. However, up to one Sidereal of her caste can support her, participating in the planning to support her. They need not have the Charm themselves. Each adds 1 to the maximum summonable Essence. The dice pool for summoning and binding the spirit starts at 0. The death of one Exalted or 20 unExalted warriors on the Sidereal's side calls to bind the spirit adds one success to this pool. Whenever the player rolls against the spirit's Essence, success binds the spirit to grant whatsoever favor the character demands and exact no retribution -- until she takes revenge it chooses. (Elder spirits often consider killing the Sidereal too crude a revenge, instead seeking to impose an equally demeaning slavery upon her.) Suicide and favors tantamount to it are outside the limits of this agreement. An army may only enact one Battle Pattern-type Charm. Sidereal Exalted can always use their Conviction with this Charm.
prerequisiteText: Presence in Absence Technique, Force Decision, Essence-Draining Battle Pattern, Demon-Blocking Battle Pattern

name: Red Haze
summary: Root Charm of the Battles Caste Resistance tree ('The Shield'); crimson starlight settles over everything the Sidereal can see, penalizing rolls by inhabitants of Malfeas/the Underworld affecting blessed things and bonusing rolls made against them.
description: Motes of crimson starlight fall in a mist over all things the character can see, warping the Essence of mortals, spirits, Exalted and even inanimate objects with furious opposition to the Primordial foe. Inhabitants of Malfeas and the Underworld lose one die from all rolls to affect creatures and places thus blessed. Rolls made defending against these enemies gain one die.

name: Someone Else's Destiny
summary: Reflexively expels the effects of a poison or drug from the Sidereal's body onto a future enemy, adding Essence in dice to the Resistance roll to avoid the substance's effects.
description: Hissing, the character expels the effects of any poison or drug affecting her, sending it onto a future enemy. Her player adds Essence in dice to a Resistance roll to avoid the substance's effects. If the roll succeeds, the substance ceases to exist, except as a memo attached to her fate. It reappears, coalescing around her enemy, a moment before the next physical attack she makes that hits, letting her player roll at least one die of lethal or aggravated damage. The full quantity of that poison or drug then enters the bloodstream of the person she hit, with its normal effects.

name: Water and Fire Legion
summary: A reflexive sacrifice of pain binds the Sidereal to fire or water for the scene, making her immune to that element's harm and letting her extend the same protection to allies and things she cares for; can also coerce a fire or water spirit into service.
description: With a reflexive sacrifice of pain, the character binds herself to the defense of fate. If she touches a flame, flame cannot burn or suffocate her for the duration of the Charm. If she touches a body of water, she cannot freeze, boil, sicken or drown her. Her allies and the things she cares for all fall under this protection. In addition, while touching a spirit or elemental of fire or water -- which may require a Brawl or Martial Arts action -- the character can reflexively invoke this Charm. Her player rolls Charisma + Resistance against a difficulty equal to the spirit's Essence to coerce it into service. This service must take the form of protecting something reasonably concrete. The Sidereal dictates what the spirit must protect. The spirit cannot retaliate for this Charm's duration. This Charm automatically expires at Calibration, and cannot be applied during that time. Sidereal Exalted may always use their Conviction with this Charm.

name: Shield of Mars
summary: Reflexively transfers incoming damage from the Sidereal (or a present ally) to one of her attacker's allies, converting each two successes rolled into one level of undodgeable, unblockable, unsoakable transferred damage, though perfect defenses on the original target block the transfer.
description: Snarling fate with a twist of her hand, the character passes damage she might have suffered on to another. After damage is rolled but before it is applied, the Sidereal's player makes a reflexive Dexterity + Resistance roll. Each two successes allow the Exalt to transfer one level of undodgeable, unblockable and unsoakable damage to her attacker or one of her attacker's allies (who need not be present) rather than taking it herself. She cannot transfer more damage than she originally took. She transfers bashing damage to others as bashing damage. She transfers lethal and aggravated damage to others as lethal damage. If her target uses a perfect dodge such as Seven Shadow Evasion, a perfect block such as the Heavenly Guardian Defense or a perfect soak Charm such as the Adamant Skin Technique, neither the target nor the Sidereal suffer the transferred damage.

name: Storm's Eye Stance
summary: Capstone of the Resistance tree; a prayer strip's afterburn tangles a number of visible targets' fates with the Sidereal's own life, undoing all damage and deleterious effects dealt to them by re-rolling the attack after the fact against her own defenses instead.
description: This Charm uses a prayer strip marked with the scripture of the One-Handed Maiden. The character casts it into the air and night's darkness falls all around her. The prayer strip burns like a hot coal, hovering near her and casting a flickering red light over the side of her face. When any effect does her harm, the Exalt can tangle the destiny of any number of visible targets with her own. This is a reflexive action costing 3 motes per target. She invokes this effect after all damage or deleterious effects at the Exalt are rolled but before they are applied. Her targets suffer the same effects the Exalt suffers as the attack. Only perfect dodges such as Seven Shadow Evasion, perfect blocks such as the Heavenly Guardian Defense or a perfect soak Charm such as the Adamant Skin Technique protect her against this attack.
prerequisiteText: Red Haze, Someone Else's Destiny, Water and Fire Legion, Shield of Mars

name: Auspicious Prospects for (Caste)
summary: One Charm that is actually five near-identical variants, one favored by each Maiden's Caste, that grants a Sidereal an intuitive sense of when and where some caste-appropriate opportunity (travel, love, war, or the world's overall direction) is coming due, plus the ability to verify other Sidereals' claims about favorable fate.
description: The Maidens grant many of their Chosen this gift, which keeps them clear-eyed and ever-alert for the patterns in the stars that inform them of the needs of destiny. It is actually five near-identical Charms, one for each Maiden: Auspicious Prospects for Journeys helps the character know when someone ought to travel, and possibly where; Auspicious Prospects for Serenity helps her locate appropriate love matches or determine whom fate wishes to have joy; Auspicious Prospects for Battles hints at when, where, and among whom a battle or war ought to take place; and Auspicious Prospects for Fate (the Maiden of Secrets' own version) gives insight into the proper overall direction of the world. This knowledge almost never gives the character a direct benefit -- more often it hands her a goal to strive for, so she must be content with the joy of service. She can also spend a mote of Essence and succeed at an Intelligence + Investigation roll to investigate another Sidereal's claim that some fate is favorable or necessary. Any Sidereal can learn any of the five variants; all five are favored (cheaper) for the Chosen of Secrets, while the other castes favor only their own caste's variant.

name: Marvelous Inclusion of Details
summary: Root Charm of the Investigation tree; adds automatic successes to an Investigation roll and lets the character choose, within reason, what kind of useful evidence she turns up.
description: On learning this Charm, the character weaves a thread of aquamarine mystery into her eyes; from then on, secrets are drawn to her the way fate favors its kin. This Charm adds successes equal to the character's Essence, automatically, to an Investigation roll. If possible, the character chooses what kind of evidence she finds -- a murder weapon, a conveniently shelved book, notes tucked inside it, footprints, or similar -- and whatever she picks, she finds it instantly. Sidereal Exalted may always use their Compassion with this Charm.

name: Efficient Secretary Technique
summary: Root Charm of the Investigation tree; conjures a tiny, indestructible spirit-spider that scurries off to fetch some single piece of mundane, non-secret information and reports back a turn later.
description: On learning this Charm, the character spits out a jubilant construct of Essence shaped like a small, unmanifested emerald pattern spider. When invoked, it races along the weave of fate to locate some fact for the character -- any available information that is neither generally lost nor actively concealed, such as the name of a local god-king, how long ago a widow lost her husband, the status of a war, or the temperature in Nexus. One turn later it returns and whispers the answer into the character's ear. The spirit is indestructible while the Exalt lives.

name: Research Assistant Invocation
summary: Grows a plant into a mortal-statted scholar-servant with strong Investigation, Awareness, Lore, and Linguistics who assists with research for five days, reverting to plant form under stress.
description: The Sidereal claps her hands, causing a small plant to grow into the shape of a dedicated scholar and observer. This creature has the statistics and appearance of a typical mortal, except that it has Intelligence 3, Awareness 3, Investigation 4, Lore 2, and Linguistics equal to the character's own. It happily assists with research and investigation in any desired subject, carrying materials and noting details the character might miss. Under stress, such as combat, it panics and reverts to plant form; it can be coaxed back into human shape by reapplying this Charm.

name: Embracing Life Method
summary: Capstone of the Investigation tree; plants a prayer strip as a seed that grows into a tree over five days, drawing wood spirits who leave gifts and information related to a question the Sidereal plants in her own mind.
description: This Charm uses a prayer strip marked with the scripture of That Old Thing. The Sidereal forms a question or curiosity in her mind and plants the strip as if it were a seed. Over the next day it develops roots and sprouts into a tall mulberry tree, drawing local wood spirits who leave small gifts or secrets behind. Five days later the Sidereal returns and her player rolls Charisma + Investigation; each success yields both a piece of information useful to her curiosity and a gift left beneath the tree, alongside various worthless offerings. Returning early for faster answers is possible but may provoke the wrath of the wood spirits.
prerequisiteText: Marvelous Inclusion of Details, Research Assistant Invocation

name: Creation Smuggling Procedures
summary: Root Charm of the Larceny tree; wraps the Sidereal's fingers in tendrils of fate that create a small pocket of Creation-stability around her, protecting her and anyone within 10 yards from the Wyld's touch.
description: The character calls the weave of events to her. Thin tendrils of fate snake out from Creation to twine around her fingers, fading into phosphorescent green visibility for the final meter of their journey. If she is in or ventures into the Wyld, she becomes a small island of Creation's stability, her destiny smuggled into the realm of chance by art and cunning. Neither she nor anything within 10 yards of her suffers the touch of the Wyld.

name: Sidereal Shell Games
summary: Lets the Sidereal steal a portion of a target's destiny, borrowing soak, damage dice, or dice from a specific pool up to her own Essence, at the target's expense for the rest of the scene.
description: The character again summons the weave of events, crossing her wrists and interweaving threads from one hand to the other as they materialize. On a successful Wits + Larceny roll, she steals a portion of her target's destiny and can borrow, up to her Essence, bashing or lethal soak, damage dice, or dice from a specific pool such as Dexterity + Melee. The target loses the use of that soak or those dice for the rest of the scene while the character gains it; she cannot borrow more than the target possesses. The Charm is partially cumulative -- she can filch different things in one scene but cannot add to the same pool twice -- and any borrowed dice count as a dice bonus from a Charm for purposes of stacking limits with other dice-bonus Charms.
cost: 1 mote + 2 motes per die or level successfully stolen, 1 Willpower

name: Name Pilfering Practices
summary: Root Charm of the Larceny tree; steals a target's true name so that only the Sidereal can speak or think it for the Charm's duration, unless the victim notices the theft in progress.
description: With a twist and a tug, the Sidereal steals another being's true name. She learns the victim's true name, and for the duration of the Charm, none but the Exalt can speak or think it. The target may make a reflexive Dexterity + Larceny roll, difficulty equal to the Sidereal's Essence, to notice the theft and substitute another name for their own before it completes.

name: Dream Confiscation Approach
summary: Follow-up to Name Pilfering Practices; on physical contact, unweaves a small measure of the target's Essence into unsoakable aggravated damage while leaving them listless and unable to regain Willpower or regenerate Essence until released.
description: Bumping casually into her target or otherwise making physical contact, and after a successful Wits + Larceny roll (difficulty equal to the target's Essence), the character pockets some of the victim's Essence as dice of aggravated damage, ignoring armor, by dexterously unweaving some of the dreams from the Essence's nature. The stolen Essence becomes ravenous and slightly mad, though sane enough to Dodge further theft attempts. Any character affected by this Charm becomes listless: until the Sidereal releases their dreams, they cannot regain Willpower and do not regenerate Essence naturally. Sidereal Exalted may always use their Temperance with this Charm.

name: Honorable Thief Spirit
summary: Root Charm of the Larceny tree; coats the Sidereal in glittering, near-invisible sparks that make her seem to have exactly the virtues rogues and scoundrels respect, reducing target numbers for peaceful or defensive dealings with them.
description: Glittering green sparks weave about the character before settling into her hair and skin, becoming all but invisible. To the eyes of any criminal, she seems to have exactly the virtues and qualities that best qualify her for respect and admiration. The Sidereal can reduce the target number of all peaceful or defensive interactions with rogues, scum, and knaves.

name: Conning Chaos Technique
summary: Capstone of the Larceny tree; a prayer strip binds a distant victim's destiny into a Wyld-fed curse whose escalating misfortune and monster attacks can only be ended by finding and destroying the strip, at the cost of marking the Sidereal as a target for the very forces she summoned.
description: This Charm uses a prayer strip marked with the scripture of the Savory Maiden. The Sidereal holds it up and it affixes itself to reality as if nailed to the air, then names a victim within 10 miles; the strip burns like a hot coal as it trades the victim's destiny for a portion of chaos claimed into Creation. The player rolls Manipulation + Larceny; each success represents one month of the resulting curse, and the Wyld's malevolent (but undirected) attention on the victim intensifies each month, drawing Fair Folk and Wyld-spawned monsters and eventually inflicting a derangement or a taint. The victim can overcome the deterioration for a scene with a successful Temperance roll, and the curse ends once the Maidens' order has reclaimed more territory from chaos than the Charm consumed -- though the Sidereal's own name becomes marked, making her more likely to be hunted by the forces she invoked the more she uses it. A victim's player can make an extended monthly Intelligence + Lore roll to understand the curse: six successes reveal that the prayer strip is somewhere within 10 miles of where the curse fell and that destroying it frees the victim, and twelve successes give its precise location.
prerequisiteText: Sidereal Shell Games, Dream Confiscation Approach, Honorable Thief Spirit

name: Systematic Understanding of Everything
summary: Root Charm of the Lore tree; the Sidereal spends the night filtering her perceptions of the Loom of Fate into a growing, sleep-only specialty in an Ability of her choice.
description: The character sleeps, and the Maiden of Secrets grants her a vision of the projected plan for fate, from the moment of her waking until the end of Creation. A character trained to use this Charm can filter her perceptions and integrate a small portion of the Loom of Fate with her own extensive knowledge, adding a +1 specialty of her choice to her next dream, applicable to all relevant Abilities. Characters can only spend Essence for this Charm while asleep; this can increase the specialty total for an Ability above +3, but the character cannot add more than three specialty dice to any given roll. These specialties are dice bonuses added by a Charm and should be considered as such when determining the maximum effect of other dice-bonus Charms.

name: The Methodology of Secrets
summary: Extends Systematic Understanding of Everything into a stronger, sleep-only specialty: +3 to one chosen Ability and +1 to all relevant Abilities.
description: This Charm extends Systematic Understanding of Everything, providing a specialty that gives a +3 bonus to one Ability and a +1 bonus to all Abilities where it is relevant. Characters can only spend Essence for this Charm while asleep, and cannot invoke it in the same slumber as Systematic Understanding of Everything. It can increase the specialty total for an Ability above +3, but the character cannot add more than three specialty dice to any given roll.

name: Of Truths Best Unspoken
summary: Lets a trinity of Sidereals (one each serving Serenity, Battles, and Secrets) jointly witness a future atrocity and later recall, once per month, how events lead toward it.
description: Scuttling on the paths of tragedy are the seven Heptarchs of Tragedy, gods of the truths and futures displeasing to mortal eyes. Catching sight of a horror to come, they snatch up knowledge of it and bind it in a living sepulcher cast into the earth. Gathering for three hours and simultaneously invoking this Charm, a trinity of Exalted serving Serenity, Battles, and Secrets can dredge such a sepulcher forth and witness an atrocity not yet come to pass. At any time within the next year, each player can make a single Lore roll as if looking backward from the end of the Age of Sorrows to recall notable events leading toward it -- five successes may lead directly to it, while one success may only confirm it will occur 'eventually.' Characters can use this Charm at most once per month, and multiple uses are not cumulative. Sidereal Exalted may always use their Conviction with this Charm.

name: Of Things Desired and Feared
summary: Lets a trinity of Sidereals (one each serving Journeys, Serenity, and Endings) jointly map a plan toward a shared goal, guaranteeing eventual success at a Storyteller-set narrative price.
description: Gathering for three hours and simultaneously invoking this Charm, a trinity of Exalted serving Journeys, Serenity, and Endings map the paths of destiny and learn at least one method by which they may achieve a shared goal. Mechanically, they learn the price of success, and their eventual victory occurs narratively among other unfolding stories; the price can range from minor setbacks to the loss of something the characters value. Characters may reasonably pursue the prophesied path, pay the price, or drop the goal instead; the Storyteller should set a modest price for a peripheral matter and a prohibitive one for automatically resolving something central to the story. Even when the price outweighs what the characters' own planning might have achieved, they are guaranteed success and can focus their effort elsewhere.

name: Of the Shape of the World
summary: Reduces target numbers on a roll by drawing on foresight of the truth the Sidereal intends to bring about.
description: Averting her eyes from the truth that is, the character invokes a truth she wishes to create, reducing the target number for a Sidereal astrology-related roll.
cost: 3 motes per target number reduction, 1 Willpower

name: Of Horrors Best Unknown
summary: Casts a slow, inescapable net of destiny around any visible creature -- even beings normally immune to fate -- that steadily worsens their circumstances for a year and a day.
description: The Sidereal weaves one of the nets of Neferuten, made from filaments of destiny thinner than the distance between a stone and its shadow. These nets can catch and cling even to things normally immune to destiny's workings -- not strong enough to impede a Primordial's course, but able to adhere to the borders of Cecelyne, the Endless Desert, or hang from a Deathlord's flesh. The Exalt can cast the net around any creature she can see; success requires a Dexterity + Lore roll against a difficulty equal to the target's Essence. Afterward, the net exerts a slow, continual pull that reduces by 1 (to a minimum of 4) the target number of any roll in circumstances opposing the target. The net lasts a year and a day; instead of rolling, the Sidereal can spend a permanent Willpower to guarantee success and ensure it lasts as long as needed. Multiple such nets may cover a single target. Sidereal Exalted may always use their Valor with this Charm.
prerequisiteText: Of the Shape of the World

name: Of Secrets Yet Untold
summary: Grants a spirit an unspeakable secret in exchange for one obligatory favor, chosen by fate rather than by either party, that restrains the spirit from initiating hostile action until repaid.
description: Hissing a long susurration, the character illumines an elemental or spirit of the earth in a verdant glow and bestows upon it a secret -- a truth about the world's long course that the spirit can never speak. The spirit must perform one favor for the Exalted in return, chosen by necessity rather than desire; neither the character nor the spirit chooses what the favor is. The character automatically knows the favor's nature, but the spirit does not. Until the favor is paid, the spirit needs a successful Wits + Temperance roll (difficulty 3) to initiate hostile action against the Exalt, though it can still reply to violence with violence.

name: Avoiding the Truth Technique
summary: A standalone root Charm usable in a Combo with Charms of other Abilities; adds automatic successes to a Socialize, Presence, or Bureaucracy roll meant to convince a listener that a true, horrifying statement is a lie.
description: Drawing on preternatural insight, the character imbues a true statement with implications that horrify the listener, then adds her Essence in automatic successes to a Socialize, Presence, or Bureaucracy roll to convince the victim she is lying. This Charm is explicitly permitted to be used in a Combo with Charms of other Abilities.

name: Transcendent Hatchet of Fate
summary: Capstone of the Lore tree; a prayer strip lets the Sidereal name a target's worst fear and make it destined fact, instantly draining the target's Willpower and Essence, though the Storyteller may substitute a different dramatic realization and later game events can still avert it.
description: This Charm uses a prayer strip marked with the scripture of the Maiden in Terror, which glows sickly green as it curls, twists, and sinks into the Sidereal's palm, leaving a faint tracery of Old Realm symbols. When she chooses, the Sidereal shows her palm to a target and names that victim's fate -- which of the target's worst fears the world will realize, and how. The Exalt's player rolls Intelligence + Lore; the target instantly loses the Sidereal's Essence plus the number of successes in temporary Willpower (to a minimum of 0), and twice that amount in motes of Essence. Ordinarily the player simply states what is now preordained, choosing a fate and manner of realization that is dramatically interesting; at the moment she speaks, that event is destined. The Storyteller should suggest an alternative if the stated destiny simply cannot come to pass, and later game events -- changes in circumstance or the meddling of Primordials -- can still alter or avert it, but the target herself cannot avoid her doom by her own action.
prerequisiteText: The Methodology of Secrets, Of Truths Best Unspoken, Of Things Desired and Feared, Of Horrors Best Unknown, Of Secrets Yet Untold, Avoiding the Truth Technique

name: Mark of Exaltation
summary: Root Charm of the Occult tree; makes the Sidereal's Caste Mark shimmer visibly to spirits and adds automatic successes to social rolls made when dealing with spirits or in Yu-Shan.
description: The character's Caste Mark shimmers, casting forth an appropriately colored light visible only to spirits and the Chosen of her caste; in addition, unrelated spirits who can see it also perceive it. This adds one automatic success to all Presence, Performance, Occult, and Bureaucracy rolls made when dealing with spirits or in Yu-Shan. This explicitly stacks with effects that give rise to dice up to the dice limit -- it exceeds it if it exceeds the dice limit. Sidereal Exalted may always use their Compassion with this Charm. Learning this Charm requires the appropriate Maiden's approval.

name: Incite Decorum
summary: Root Charm of the Occult tree; invokes the Maiden's blessing so that weaker spirits and elementals must spend extra Willpower to act against the Sidereal, at an added Willpower cost to any Charms they use in the conflict.
description: Invoking the blessing of his Maiden, the character facilitates polite dealings with the spirit world. Spirits and elementals with the Sidereal's Essence or lower must spend 2 temporary Willpower to initiate hostile action against the character; in addition, each Charm they use in a conflict they initiate against him costs 1 additional Willpower, including Charms that do not normally cost Willpower. Learning this Charm requires the appropriate Maiden's approval.

name: Tell-Tale Symphony
summary: Follow-up to Mark of Exaltation; lets the Sidereal (and other nearby Sidereals) hear a soft musical tone given off by nearby Essence patterns, revealing hidden spirits and active Charms or sorcery.
description: To help the character better untangle the threads of fate, the patterns of Essence around her -- Charms, sorcery, and other effects -- give rise to strange but fitting melodies. Spirits, manifested or otherwise, emit a soft and inadvertent noise, like the ringing of bells. Only Sidereal Exalted within earshot can hear this music. Both the character and other Sidereals within earshot can automatically detect the presence of enchantments and unmanifested spirits. An Intelligence + Occult roll against difficulty 3 allows Sidereal Exalted with this Charm to identify the details of an enchantment or the approximate rank and job description of a spirit, or the minutiae of the local geomantic environment.

name: Innocuous Maneuver
summary: Follow-up combining Mark of Exaltation and Incite Decorum; lets the Sidereal call in a favor from a supernatural patron to sway a target, at the cost of drawing scrutiny if abused too often.
description: Wrapped in the terrible grandeur of the Maiden that sponsors her, the Sidereal can present a compelling case for her intentions. If her player succeeds at a Charisma + Occult roll against a difficulty equal to the target's Essence, the Exalt acquires a spirit's support in some political matter, even one diametrically opposed to the target. The Sidereal can attempt this Charm at most once per year against a given target. When used to lose a celestial audit, each use of this Charm counts as an independent Severity 1 offense; when used on the winning side, there is no penalty (helping others agree with the censor's final opinion defines the crime). Sidereal Exalted may always use their Valor with this Charm. Learning this Charm requires the appropriate Maiden's approval.

name: Unweaving Method
summary: Capstone of the Occult tree's Sorcerer I branch; corrupts a target's pattern of existence with the essence of chaos and endings, dealing unsoakable, undodgeable aggravated damage that cannot harm the dead.
description: Sidereals with a deep understanding of the ways of the Wyld and the dead can apply it to their manipulation of fate. With a deft touch on the weave, the character corrupts the pattern of a person's existence with the essence of chaos and endings, inflicting her Essence in dice of unsoakable aggravated damage on any creature or object she can see. This damage cannot be blocked or dodged. The Unweaving Method cannot harm the dead and has no effect on characters or items shielded from the influence of the Wyld.

name: Terrestrial Circle Sorcery
summary: Root Charm of the Occult tree's Sorcerer II branch; grants access to learn and cast a single Terrestrial Circle sorcery spell, whose own Essence cost is paid separately.
description: For the Sidereal Exalted, steeped in the lore of the First Age, Terrestrial Circle Sorcery comes easily. Invoking this Charm only enables the character to cast a single Terrestrial Circle spell; the spell itself has an Essence cost, often very high, that the character must pay to actualize it. This Charm can never be part of a Combo.
reviewFlags: Compatibility text reads 'Duration: Simple' in the source stat block, echoing its own Type wording rather than a distinct Duration value; possible source inconsistency, transcribed as printed (matches the inventory row's own note).

name: Celestial Circle Sorcery
summary: Follow-up to Terrestrial Circle Sorcery; grants access to a single Celestial Circle spell, requiring the sacrifice of one prayer strip the first time it is cast.
description: Those Sidereal Exalted who attain the pinnacle of one constellation's Charms, learning to understand and use one of the scriptures found upon the Maidens' Loom, unlock a path in their minds through which they may learn Celestial Circle sorcery. The first time they cast a Celestial Circle spell, they must also sacrifice a prayer strip inscribed with the scripture of the Maiden in Chains, which burns away in a gout of emerald fire. Celestial Circle Sorcery can never be part of a Combo.
prerequisiteText: Terrestrial Circle Sorcery, one prayer strip Charm

name: Soft Presence Practice
summary: Root Charm of the Stealth tree; reduces the target number of any roll made to remain undetected for a scene.
description: The natural residents of Creation deform the flow of others' fates, marking it with the signs of their presence. Using this Charm, the character reduces this deformation, stepping lightly through the world the Maidens weave. For one scene, she reduces the target number of any roll to remain undetected.

name: Blinding the Boar
summary: Root Charm of the Stealth tree; makes the Sidereal undetectable to anyone without Essence of their own, and imposes a target number penalty on supernatural trackers.
description: Quiet as the Void, the Sidereal steps entirely out of the weave of fate. Only those with Essence greater than her own can sense her directly; a reflexive Perception + Awareness roll allows others without that edge to feel her presence nearby, and even on success they suffer a +2 difficulty penalty on attempts to attack or affect her while she uses this Charm. Only supernatural trackers can engage in tracking contests with her. If the Sidereal's anima banner becomes visible, the Charm instantly fails. For its duration, the Sidereal is treated as a creature outside of fate. Learning this Charm requires the Maiden of Secrets' approval.

name: Walking Outside Fate
summary: Follow-up to Soft Presence Practice; a subtler, indefinite-duration version that keeps the Sidereal beneath fate's notice as long as she does not use her anima banner.
description: Quiet as the Void, the Sidereal steps entirely out of the weave of fate. Only those with Essence greater than her own can sense her directly; the touch of chance allows others to feel a presence nearby with a reflexive Perception + Awareness roll, and even on success they suffer a +2 difficulty penalty on attempts to attack or affect her. If they succeed, they cannot engage in tracking contests with her unless they are supernatural trackers. The Charm fails instantly if the Sidereal returns to the weave of fate by making her anima banner visible. For the duration of this Charm, the Sidereal is treated as a creature outside of fate. Learning this Charm requires the Maiden of Secrets' approval.

name: Subordinate Inspiration Technique
summary: Follow-up to Walking Outside Fate; plants a thought in a target's mind that they perceive as their own idea, undetectable except by an unusually perceptive listener.
description: The character can use this Charm only while Walking Outside Fate. Any spirit or Sidereal present hears the character's words as if they were her own thoughts. A target must succeed at a Perception + Awareness roll against a difficulty equal to the Sidereal's Essence to realize the thoughts are not her own.

name: Ceasing to Exist Approach
summary: Capstone of the Stealth tree; a prayer strip lets the Sidereal erase her old identity and instantly assume a wholly new one -- appearance, Backgrounds, and social relationships included -- indistinguishable from a Charm-suitable native of that new life.
description: This Charm uses a prayer strip marked with the scripture of Absence. The character places it on her chest, where it flashes with dark green light and wraps around her heart; in that instant the Sidereal vanishes from the weave of fate and reappears elsewhere, woven seamlessly into a new life. The character creates a new identity and appearance for herself as any sort of non-Primordial creature -- mortal, Exalted, spirit, or the dead -- though she cannot become someone who already exists. She chooses up to 15 dots of Backgrounds appropriate to her new life (Background dots above 3 cost double), travels instantly to a location chosen by the Maiden of Secrets to fit her new identity, and instantly develops appropriate social relationships, seamlessly integrating into the life of any appropriate entity save creatures of the Wyld and spirits on or above the level of the Maidens. The character does not gain new Abilities. When possible, others perceive her Charms and anima as effects suitable to her new self. If the Sidereal dismisses this Charm or spends more than 10 motes of Peripheral Essence, the Charm ends; its effects linger for five days afterward, after which the Sidereal snaps back to her old identity and its appropriate location.
prerequisiteText: Subordinate Inspiration Technique, Blinding the Boar

name: Burn Life
summary: Root Charm of the Athletics tree; sacrifices future lifespan and Essence to temporarily boost Strength, Dexterity, or Stamina beyond the Sidereal's Essence rating.
description: The character draws upon the long thread of his own future for power, sacrificing a few days or weeks of lifespan to suffuse his physical form with Essence. His player rolls Essence + Athletics; each success adds one point that the Exalt can add to his Strength, Dexterity or Stamina until the end of the scene, up to more than his Essence. Each increase costs 3 motes of Essence and three days of lifespan; successes not paid for are lost. Increases to his Attributes are dice bonuses added by a Charm and should be considered as such when determining the maximum effect of other dice-bonus Charms. Sidereal Exalted may always use their Conviction with this Charm.
cost: 3 motes + 3 days of lifespan per Attribute point purchased

name: Forgotten Earth
summary: Root Charm of the Athletics tree; cuts the Sidereal's connection to the ground for an instant, tripling her leaping distance for a single jump.
description: For a moment, the character cuts the connection between herself and the ground, and her destiny lies in the air. She triples her leaping distance for a single jump.

name: Inexorable Advance
summary: Root Charm of the Athletics tree; smooths out the character's own moments of motion so her movements ignore normal wound and armor penalties that reduce movement for five turns.
description: Eliding the moments of her own life between footsteps, or between the beginning of a gesture and the need for motion, the character suffers no wound or armor penalties of any sort, nor any penalties that reduce her running speed. With a few days' practice, characters first learning this Charm find their movements involve flickering shifts in their position, as if others saw them through a strobe light; with more practice, they can smooth out this effect, moving with a fluid grace that appears to ignore normal anatomical constraints.

name: Hungry Touch
summary: Follow-up to Burn Life; a single blow consumes an object's destiny to speed its destruction, or lets the character buy additional damage dice against a living target.
description: With a single blow, the character consumes the destiny of an object, bringing that destiny pathway toward or immediately to its final conclusion. When attempting to destroy an object with a feat of strength, the character can use this Charm to reduce the target number of the Willpower roll to boost her Strength + Athletics roll; if she succeeds at destroying the object, she recovers the Willpower point spent. Alternately, when attacking, the character can buy up to her Essence in additional points of damage at 1 mote each.
cost: 1 mote per target number reduction or damage point

name: Invisible Motion
summary: Capstone of the Athletics tree; a prayer strip lets the character reduce armor's fatigue penalty to zero and split a bonus number of automatic actions among her physical actions each turn.
description: This Charm uses a prayer strip marked with the scripture of the Maiden and the Dust. The character wraps it around her forehead or neck, whereupon it exudes a soft scent of lilacs and decay. For the rest of the day, she gains the benefits of the Inexorable Advance Charm every turn -- continuous simplification of her movements reduces the fatigue value of her armor by two, to a minimum of zero, so that a fatigue value of zero means the character never rolls to see if she becomes fatigued from wearing that armor. In addition, she doubles her movement rate and receives a number of automatic successes equal to her Athletics score to divide, in any fashion, among her physical actions each turn.
prerequisiteText: Hungry Touch, Forgotten Earth, Inexorable Advance

name: Prior Warning
summary: Root Charm of the Awareness tree; a standing Essence commitment gives the Sidereal an early, wordless feeling of unease whenever danger is approaching.
description: Once a Sidereal commits Essence to this Charm, her perceptions constantly probe the immediate future for anything that could harm her. When the character is in danger, her player makes a reflexive Wits + Awareness roll; on success she feels a warning ill ease for two minutes per success rolled. This Charm only spots obvious, imminent harm -- a slow-acting poison in her ale would not trigger it until just before it took effect, though that timing still gives her a chance to deduce the cause and seek a cure.

name: Expected Pain
summary: Follow-up to Prior Warning; automatically activates with one turn's notice whenever something dangerous or awful is about to happen, naming its general nature and voiding ambushes.
description: The character has a general sense of the bad things that will happen to him over his life; when an unpleasant moment impends, that awareness crystallizes. This Charm activates automatically when something unexpectedly dangerous or awful is about to happen, and the character learns its general nature ('attack,' 'poison,' 'betrayal,' 'loss of loved one,' 'humiliation'). He has one turn's warning in which to turn his fate aside. Ambushes against the character automatically fail, though he does not automatically detect his attacker.

name: Wise Choice
summary: Root Charm of the Awareness tree; grants a brief glimpse into which of several options offers the best short-term outcome, without revealing longer-term consequences.
description: Life is full of choices. This Charm gives a Sidereal the edge on many by letting him make the best choice when confronted with several options. The Charm only allows a brief peek into the immediate future, not into all the long-term consequences of a decision; the ideal short-term outcome is guaranteed, but long-term gains are not.

name: Supernal Awareness
summary: Follow-up to Expected Pain; lets the Sidereal continuously monitor several vague-but-identifiable disturbances (specific people, spirits, or phenomena) within a wide radius for a scene, without relying on any physical sense.
description: The character can see the web of fate around her as it cascades into the unavoidable reality of the present. She can focus attention on the influx of destiny to watch continuously, out to a distance of her Essence times 100 yards, for specific disturbances -- tracking people within that region, monitoring spirits, or watching for a phenomenon such as combat, Essence use, or the mention of her name. She senses only vague details: she can identify the location and rough power level of what she recognizes but not the course of events, and only Charms or effects she is already familiar with register clearly (an unfamiliar Charm might register only as being of a certain Essence rating). The effect is cumulative -- five uses in a scene let her monitor five different things. It does not rely on any of the character's senses, so ordinary Stealth or invisibility/silence Charms have no effect on it.

name: Inevitable Pursuit
summary: Root Charm of the Awareness tree; tracks a target across a day-old (or, in populous areas, hour-old) trail by reading the impressions their passage leaves on the destinies of everything nearby rather than physical signs.
description: No one can hide from their past. This Charm unwinds events inevitably, cascading from the past into the present and into an inescapable collection of destinies. The character tracks targets not by physical marks but by the impressions their passage leaves on the destinies of everything around them. In a relatively uninhabited region she can follow a trail as old as one day per point of her permanent Essence; in a more populous region, where many overlapping destinies interact chaotically, she is limited to trails no older than one hour per point of Essence. This ability can be foiled by the Traceless Passage Charm or similar effects; if the target used such a Charm, the matter is resolved as a standard opposed tracking contest.

name: Conclusive Wisdom
summary: Capstone of the Awareness tree; a prayer strip forces a target to live through a vivid, consequence-free vision of their own likely death, with lasting Willpower or trait damage if they fail to keep their nerve.
description: This Charm uses a prayer strip marked with the scripture of the Maiden and the Scythe. The character holds it up before her target; it fixes in the air and blossoms with pungent violet flowers whose petals dry and turn to dust over the following seconds. The target is transported into a vision of a likely ending for his life, set a few hours, minutes, or turns before its conclusion. He rolls his permanent Willpower against difficulty 3: success means the vision only faces him with no lasting effect, while failure leaves him deeply shaken, reduces his temporary Willpower to 1, and empties his Essence pool (reducing temporary Essence by his Personal Essence, to a minimum of 0) for the rest of the scene. The Storyteller plays out an appropriate death scenario, which the target can alter in one small way per point of permanent Essence he possesses; resources spent or recovered within the vision do not affect his real totals. If he survives the vision through roleplay, luck, or cleverness, he generally recovers his full temporary Willpower a few scenes later. If he dies in the vision having passed his permanent Willpower roll, he suffers no permanent ill effect but disquiet; if he dies having failed it, he must roll his temporary and permanent Willpower (spending no Willpower on the roll), and failure on either roll costs one dot of an appropriate Trait (minimum 1) and locks him out of his Personal Essence pool for the rest of the story, leaving only Peripheral Essence. This Charm has no effect on Abyssal Exalted or the dead, but it does affect Second and Third Circle demons despite their usual immunity to Willpower loss from Sidereal Charms.
prerequisiteText: Supernal Awareness, Wise Choice, Inevitable Pursuit

name: Slick Essence Replenishment
summary: Root Charm of the Bureaucracy tree; a passive Charm that refunds Essence after a Sidereal successfully uses Temperance or lands a Bureaucracy roll that advances her agenda.
description: In demonstrating her superiority to the frantic masses that mill about her, a calm and settled soul becomes a natural sinkhole for the Essence of the world. This Charm draws on a Sidereal's ability to keep perspective and maintain her tranquility in the most troubled circumstances, easily juggling a hundred projects and a thousand data points, controlling herself always and controlling others when necessary. Immediately after a successful roll using Temperance, or immediately after a Bureaucracy roll that substantially helps her implement her agenda, the Exalt regains twice her Temperance in motes of Essence, up to her normal maximum. There is no cost to use this Charm's effect -- learning this Charm simply enhances the Exalt's capabilities.

name: Icy Hand
summary: Root Charm of the Bureaucracy tree; a cold touch that drives away bureaucratic corruption, compelling a touched bureaucrat to perform his duties honestly.
description: The character's cold, clean touch instantly drives away bureaucratic corruption. She can invoke this Charm immediately after touching a target bureaucrat, which, for unwilling targets, requires an unarmed attack (which need do no damage). The Sidereal's player rolls Charisma + Bureaucracy against the target's Essence. If successful, the target is compelled to perform his duties honestly for the duration of the Charm. A spark in the character's pupil glitters violet during the use of this Charm.

name: Underling Invisibility Practice
summary: Root Charm of the Bureaucracy tree; renders the Sidereal invisible to anyone who looks down on the Chosen or considers themselves the character's superior.
description: By the will of the Maiden of Endings, who marks the end to every destiny, those who consider themselves above the process of fate find themselves most vulnerable to it. With this Charm, the character conceals his presence effectively from those who foolishly consider themselves his superiors: anyone who knows of the Sidereal Exalted and looks down upon them, or who considers himself superior to all others, simply cannot detect the Sidereal. The character instead registers on such an entity's senses only as a brief impression tied to his caste (a sense of somewhere to be for Journeys, peace and happiness for Serenity, intangible tension for Battles, déjà vu for Secrets, or a vague air of danger for Endings). Victims can still derive secondhand information from reports of the character's direct visual impression, and can even target the Sidereal based on that faint impression, but their dice pools for detecting or defending against the Sidereal start at 0 before Charms apply. A perfect counter to invisibility overcomes this effect, and it conceals the Sidereal's tracks for only the last few seconds of travel. This Charm has no effect on other Sidereal Exalted; the Storyteller decides whether a Storyteller character falls victim to it, though players of non-Sidereals may decide their own characters' opinions of the Sidereal Exalted explicitly. Learning this Charm requires the Maiden of Endings' approval.

name: Terminal Sanction
summary: Follow-up to Icy Hand; files a Bureau of Endings petition against a spirit, elemental, or demon that forces it to manifest and, on success, opens it to destruction, binding, or coercion.
description: Sometimes, all it takes to kill a god is a word in the right ear. To invoke this Charm, the Exalt's player rolls Charisma + Bureaucracy against a difficulty equal to the target's Essence. Normally this files a petition in the Bureau of Endings, activating perquisites of the Chosen of Fate that facilitate quick, effective resolution of a conflict with a spirit or elemental; due to the terms of the Primordials' surrender, the Charm specifically affects demons of all Circles and adds the Sidereal's Essence in automatic successes against them. Whether the character succeeds or fails, the spirit must instantly manifest to meet the Sidereal's calm gaze and cannot dematerialize until the end of the scene. If the character succeeds, the spirit becomes additionally vulnerable: if its materialized body dies that scene, the Sidereal can destroy it utterly, bind it into an object, coerce it into service for a year and a day, or command its obedience for the rest of the scene, offering a second opportunity to bind a demon that breaks free of her control. Sidereal Exalted may always use their Temperance with this Charm. Learning this Charm requires the Maiden of Endings' approval.

name: End Debate
summary: Capstone of the Bureaucracy tree; a prayer strip drains the desire to argue from everyone present, can halt any bureaucratic process cold, or permanently corrupt-proofs a single bureaucrat.
description: This Charm uses a prayer strip marked with the scripture of the Maiden's Promise, which explodes in searing amethyst light as the character throws it to the ground. As the light fades, passion and the desire for speech drain from all those who witnessed the Charm -- everything has already been said. Alternately, as long as one or more key individuals are present, End Debate can stop any bureaucratic process cold; only an Intelligence + Bureaucracy roll with a difficulty equal to twice the character's permanent Essence can restart it. Finally, if the Sidereal's player successfully rolls Strength + Bureaucracy against the target's Essence, this Charm can impose the effect of Icy Hand on a single bureaucrat permanently -- only by resigning his position (and, if desired, seeking another) can he re-establish a course of corruption. Sidereal Exalted may always use their Temperance with this Charm.

name: Secrets of Future Strife
summary: Root Charm of the Martial Arts tree; a permanent training effect that doubles the character's base initiative on the first turn he acts in any combat.
description: The character trains himself for instant acceptance of the twists and turns of circumstance. In any given combat, on the first turn he acts, he doubles his base initiative (Dexterity + Wits); Charms such as Opportune Shot and Thunderclap Rush Attack do not automatically win initiative over him. These advantages cease to apply once he takes his first non-reflexive action. There is no use to combine this Charm -- learning it permanently enhances the Exalt's capabilities.

name: Flight of Mercury
summary: Follow-up to Secrets of Future Strife; spends Essence to add points to the character's initiative for the rest of the scene, up to a cap of her Martial Arts score.
description: The character moves with the swift precision of one who knows her destiny. For each mote of Essence spent, she adds one point to her initiative for the remainder of the scene. Multiple applications of this Charm are cumulative, but she cannot add more than her Martial Arts score to her initiative with any combination of effects that includes this Charm.

name: Blade of the Battle Maiden
summary: Follow-up to Secrets of Future Strife; wreathes the character's hands or weapons in crimson Essence, adding dice to unarmed attacks and parries and letting her safely parry lethal blows.
description: Essence shines around the character's hands (or weapons), tracing crimson trails through the air with her every movement. For each 2 motes spent, the character adds one die to each unarmed Martial Arts attack and parry she makes for the remainder of the scene. Multiple applications of this Charm are cumulative, but she cannot more than double her normal Dexterity + Martial Arts pool with any combination of effects. While under this effect, her hands may safely parry even lethal damage blows, although blocking arrows or magical attacks requires a well-described stunt.

name: Joy in Adversity Stance
summary: Follow-up to Secrets of Future Strife; converts successful blocks and dodges into recovered Essence, letting the character profit from surviving danger.
description: Those who routinely face terrible odds can learn to take some measure of happiness in each moment's survival. Once this Charm is activated, the player rolls the Sidereal's Essence each time the character successfully blocks or dodges an attack; each success recovers two motes of Essence, flavored by the tang of Serenity. This Charm does not activate against attacks not truly intended to harm the Sidereal, nor against attacks from enemies too weak to do her any real harm.

name: Violet Bier of Sorrows Form
summary: Mid-tree Form Charm (also called the Endings Form); drains a point of a struck opponent's Virtues per successful unarmed attack and guarantees a minimum damage-dice count for the rest of the scene.
description: The character adopts the cold detachment with which Saturn marks her Sign against those things whose time has passed. While using this Form, each successful unarmed Martial Arts attack also drains one point of the victim's Virtues, to a minimum of 1 -- similar to a Solar's Virtue Flaw such as Compassionate Martyrdom. This Form cannot reduce a target's Virtues below the minimums required for the Great Curse, nor can it reduce a spirit's, elemental's, or demon's Virtue below the level needed to use a Charm (in which case the spirit loses access to that Charm until its Virtue recovers); drained Virtue heals at a rate of one point a day. This Form also changes the normal minimum for damage dice: while it is active, after a successful and potentially damaging unarmed Martial Arts attack, the character always rolls at least her Martial Arts score in damage dice. This Charm is also called the 'Endings Form.'
prerequisiteText: Flight of Mercury, Blade of the Battle Maiden, Joy in Adversity Stance

name: Death-Parrying Stroke
summary: Follow-up to Violet Bier of Sorrows Form; retroactively converts a failed parry into a partially successful one, reducing the damage taken.
description: In a blur of violet Essence, the character's hand catches an attack that might otherwise have killed him. If the character tries and fails to parry a blockable attack, he may decide -- after damage is rolled -- to invoke this Charm, reducing the damage by one health level per 2 motes spent.

name: Life-Severing Blow
summary: Follow-up to Violet Bier of Sorrows Form; lets the character buy extra automatic damage successes on a successful unarmed hit, sharable in a Combo with Brawl Charms.
description: Drawing on the Essence of Endings, a character can add power to a blow that he realizes is about to pierce his enemy's defenses. As soon as he hits an opponent with an unarmed attack, his player may declare use of this Charm at a cost of 2 motes each, purchasing more automatic successes than his character's Essence would normally allow. This Charm applies to unarmed Brawl attacks and is explicitly permitted to share a Combo with Brawl Charms; the disciplined approach of a martial artist is necessary only in the last instant of the blow.

name: Metal Storm
summary: Follow-up to Life-Severing Blow; spends Essence for extra unarmed attacks against a single target, up to the character's Martial Arts score, without splitting her dice pool.
description: Not even the most cunning of opponents can evade a sword that strikes everywhere at once. For each 3 motes spent, the character can make an extra unarmed Martial Arts attack at her full dice pool against the same target. All her attacks must be made against the same target; she cannot make more total attacks than her Martial Arts score, nor can she split her dice pool in the same turn she uses Metal Storm.

name: Conclusion-Pursuing Approach
summary: Capstone of the Martial Arts tree; grants Willpower for harming a foe and triples their wound penalties against the character, optionally enhanced with a prayer strip that drains a struck target's Willpower or Essence.
description: At the pinnacle of the Violet Bier of Sorrows Style, a character learns to draw strength from the pain of others; her attacks gain resolve as her enemy falters. She is trained to take full advantage of the weakness of the wounded, stalking failing prey as death hunts those whose time has come. Whenever she successfully harms an opponent with an unarmed Martial Arts attack, she gains one point of Willpower, and an opponent's wound penalties are tripled when it comes to attacking her or defending against her unarmed Martial Arts attacks. Sidereal Exalted, and those who learn this Charm as a Sidereal Charm, can enhance it with a prayer strip marked with the scripture of the Expectant Maiden: fixed to her sword (or other allowed weapon), it wraps the whole in radiant burgundy light. While the prayer strip survives, her weapon cannot be destroyed, and each successful Martial Arts attack subtracts a Willpower point from the target; creatures outside of fate and targets with 0 Willpower instead lose 10 motes of Essence, or, if they lack that much Essence, have all their damage dice converted to automatic successes instead.

name: Smooth Transition
summary: Root Charm of the Medicine tree; a perfect effect that instantly and painlessly kills an Incapacitated or dying target so that it cannot rise as an undead, and banishes possessed ghosts.
description: This Charm speeds and ensures a smooth transition from life to death. It instantly and painlessly kills any Incapacitated or dying target; the target cannot rise again as an undead. If applied to a corpse, neither the body nor its spirit can rise again as an undead, and zombies collapse instantly. This power cannot target ghosts directly, but if applied to a ghost's original body -- not a body it happens to possess -- it banishes the ghost instantly and permanently to the Underworld. No Charm or ability protects the victim against Smooth Transition, and it is a perfect effect. However, unusual corpses (such as spine chains) require a Charisma + Medicine roll with difficulty equal to the Essence of the creature that raised them. If the body of a target of this Charm is ever placed on naked earth or stone, it sinks quietly beneath the surface, arranging for its own burial.

name: Peaceable Conclusion
summary: Follow-up to Smooth Transition; a consensual perfect-kill effect that requires the target to genuinely wish to die, unforced and undrugged, when given time and comfort to decide.
description: As with Smooth Transition, this Charm instantly, painlessly, and perfectly kills its target. The target need not be dying, Incapacitated, or even wounded, but must be willing to pass into death; this consent cannot be forced, nor can it be forcibly withheld -- the target dies if and only if he would decide to consent, given adequate time and comfort in which to think, while under the influence of neither drug nor Charm. The Sidereal Exalted can freely make the prospect of life as unpleasant as she desires. Sidereal Exalted may always use their Valor with this Charm.

name: Invocation of the Storm-Following Silence
summary: Follow-up to Smooth Transition; extends Smooth Transition's effect to everyone within a wide radius at once, keyed to a roll compared against the raising Deathlord or deathknight's Essence for unusual corpses.
description: The character casts forth the violet radiance of Endings, bringing stillness to the weave of fate. He brings a Smooth Transition to all those within (his Essence x 10) yards. The Exalt's player makes an Intelligence + Medicine roll; when facing unusual corpses, his player instead makes a single Charisma + Medicine roll, comparing the number of successes rolled against the Essence of the Deathlord or deathknight who raised each given corpse to determine whether that corpse can rise. Sidereal Exalted may always use their Valor with this Charm.

name: Terminate Illness
summary: Root Charm of the Medicine tree; ends the natural course of a non-spiritual disease outright, killing its animating lesser god and letting the target begin recovery.
description: The character makes the Inferior Sign of the Corpse against the spirit of an illness, and it comes to its natural end. The Exalt's player makes an Intelligence + Medicine roll against the normal difficulty to treat the disease, adding his Essence in dice. If successful, the disease's course ends, the lesser god of the infection dies peacefully, and the target can begin recovery. This does not affect spiritual diseases. Sidereal Exalted may always use their Conviction with this Charm.

name: Earth and Sky Bargain
summary: Capstone of the Medicine tree; a prayer strip buries a dying earth or air spirit's Essence within the character, letting her regenerate health and gain soak for as long as she sustains the bargain, and later transfer the bound entity to another host.
description: This Charm uses a prayer strip marked with the scripture of the Maiden and the Road.
